close_reason: Duplicate of PKIX-rb6n which already tracks the empty-input panic guard removal upon x509-cert 0.3.x bump. The action (drop the BEGIN_BOUNDARY pre-scan + simplify NoCertificates handling) is the same; no separate work item needed.
description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:324-329 scans the entire input via bytes.windows(BEGIN_BOUNDARY.len()).any(...) before calling load_pem_chain, which then performs its own scan internally.

For a 3 MB Debian bundle this is ~3 million byte comparisons before parsing begins. Cheap in absolute terms (~ a few milliseconds even on slow hardware) but it is a full pre-scan that will be obsoleted as soon as the workspace bumps to x509-cert 0.3.x (the bead PKIX-rb6n already tracks the workaround-removal).

Not a real efficiency concern in the current shape because:
  - The trust-store load is a once-at-startup operation, not a hot path.
  - The pre-scan is necessary today to dodge the x509-cert 0.2.5 underflow panic.

Reason to file: when PKIX-rb6n closes (x509-cert 0.3.x bump), the entire empty-input guard becomes vestigial. The follow-up issue should track *removing* the guard, not just leaving it as belt-and-braces, so that the cost is dropped and the rustdoc claim ("returns NoCertificates when the input parsed cleanly but contained zero PEM blocks") becomes accurate again.
title: Empty-input guard duplicates load_pem_chain's whitespace-stripped emptiness check
